Contributed to shipped titles and participated in a full dev cycle from concept through release. Experience with Maya, Unreal Engine 5, including Blueprint and other gameplay implementation tools, to create and iterate on gameplay features. Excellent collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team and provide clear guidance to designers, engineers, and artists. DashMart is a local-fulfillment center owned and operated by DoorDash, offering customers fast, reliable, and high quality delivery. jobs.description: TL;DR You're a communications professional who can plan and execute the work that advances Lovable's objectives across EU and Swedish policy environments, making sure our voice is heard on the issues that matter most. You'll pair sharp corporate communications with real policy fluency — working closely with internal teams and external partners to help policymakers, media, and other stakeholders understand Lovable's perspective on the key files and issues that shape the environment we operate in. This is a balanced role, equal parts policy operator and corporate communicator. You'll report to the European Communications and Public Affairs Lead. WHY LOVABLE? Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started. We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software. WHAT YOU'LL DO This role makes sure Lovable has a credible, constructive voice in the rooms that matter — building a presence worth listening to and developing clear positions that reflect what Lovable actually builds and believes. Advocate Lovable's positions on key policy files. You'll build and run our engagement with policy representatives across EU and Swedish institutions. Own corporate communications on policy issues. Statements, briefings, op-eds, speaking moments, and the proactive announcements that build credibility over time. You'll develop the strategy, write the materials, manage media relationships, and make sure each piece reinforces the others. Track the regulatory agenda and turn it into a point of view. You'll monitor the files that affect us and develop clear positions that reflect the company's reality and ambitions. Build coalitions and work through industry. You'll represent Lovable in trade associations and industry groups, finding shared causes that move issues forward. Act as a comms and policy partner to our cross-functional team. You'll work closely with the communications and cross-functional teams in preparing for engagements with policymakers, institutions, and press, strengthening the company’s voice in the European AI debate. WHO YOU ARE You've operated in and around the policy world. That might mean an EU institution, a trade association, a think tank, or a public affairs firm. Wherever you've been, you know how a file moves from idea to law, and you can read the politics, formal and informal, that determine what actually happens. You understand policy and can communicate it. You have experience from both policy work and corporate communications, and you're equally comfortable speaking to policymakers and media alike. You can drive an issue forward in a complex political environment. You're comfortable with ambiguity and competing agendas, and you know how to prioritize when everything feels urgent. You're a sharp writer with editorial judgment. You can turn a dense regulatory development into a crisp briefing, opinion piece or clean position statement. You connect dots that other people don't see. You look at a piece of draft legislation and think ahead on what it means for the industry as well as what Lovable should say and to whom. You're a genuine cross-functional collaborator. You work easily with cross-functional stakeholders, external partners, and coalitions. You don't wait to be invited into the room. You're not precious about who gets credit. You just make things work. You're deeply curious about AI, technology policy, and the industry landscape. You keep up with what happens in the world instinctively — the news, the regulatory moves, the debates as they unfold. You understand where the conversation is heading well enough to spot a risk or an opportunity before someone hands it to you. WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW This is not a role where you set the strategy and hand off execution. You'll be writing the first drafts of our position statements, building the relationships and showing up in the room as a Lovable representative. We move fast and plans change. The job runs on two clocks at once: you'll react to the urgent issue that lands today while building the relationships and positions that set us up for success in the long term. If you need a settled environment with predictable workflows, this will be frustrating. If you find that kind of pace energizing, you'll love it. We're building public affairs and communications at a company that is itself being built. That means you'll have real influence over how this function develops in Europe: the positions, the relationships, the standards. That's the upside of being early. Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you're deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn't technically "yours" when the moment calls for it. ABOUT YOUR APPLICATION Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join. We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

You'll be a subject matter expert on copyright, privacy, data use, and AI regulation (including the EU AI Act, U.S. state laws, and emerging global rules), and will work directly with researchers on questions that often have no settled answer.
The ideal candidate will have navigated complex legal questions at the intersection of machine learning, data, and academic research in a fast-moving technical environment, with the judgment to work at the cutting edge of AI development while effectively solving issues, enabling innovation, and calibrating risk. This is a uniquely positioned role touching many different facets of AI, presenting the opportunity to be a leader in AI legal thought.

Advise research and data teams on data sourcing, licensing, partnerships, and use, and help shape Anthropic's data acquisition and use strategy as laws and markets evolve
Help coordinate regulatory readiness and model launches, review model documentation and system cards, respond to regulatory inquiries, and advise on legal questions for pre-release and internal models
Support the Responsible Scaling Policy as applied to biological and chemical risk, including capability evaluations, tiered access for biosecurity researchers, and dual-use research questions
Counsel the Societal Impacts, Economic, Alignment, Interpretability, Model Welfare, and Beneficial Deployments teams on research design, data collection and sharing, external collaborations, program launches, and publication review
Monitor global AI, privacy, copyright, and export-control developments and translate them into practical internal guidance and policy, working closely with Product, Policy, and other legal stakeholders
Engage with academics, regulators, industry groups, and civil society to help develop norms and best practices for responsible AI development and data governance

Practical, creative problem-solving: the ability to apply legal requirements to fast-changing, deeply technical work, with an understanding that the goal is to enable responsible research and product development in a risk-calibrated environment
Exceptional communication and analytical skills, technical fluency, and the ability to navigate ambiguous and uncharted legal territory, turning complex technical and legal analysis into advice people can act on
Familiarity and comfort advising on the EU AI Act, U.S. legislation and AI frameworks, GDPR/CCPA, and comparable regimes globally, sometimes where no AI-specific legislation exists
Interest in thinking deeply about the impact of AI on society and how to make humanity's transition to the AI age as beneficial as possible
Sound judgment about when to be flexible and when to hold a line; comfort making high-stakes calls in unsettled areas and outside your core expertise; and a low-ego, collaborative approach, doing the work needed rather than delegating it or being territorial

MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN Maintenance Technician – Site Minor Works Position Summary The Maintenance Technician supports the installation and relocation of laboratory instrumentation and equipment. The role provides hands-on execution for laboratory and facility Site Minor Works, including equipment moves, decommissioning, and asset tracking, while coordinating contractors, vendors, and site support teams. The position maintains equipment and asset records, supports compliance and safety requirements, and keeps stakeholders informed from project intake through closeout. Essential Duties and Responsibilities · Escort, hand-move, unpack, install, and remove laboratory and facility equipment. · Assess site preparation requirements and connect utilities, including electrical, gas, water, and data, for new and relocated instrumentation. · Coordinate relocation logistics and perform pre-move documentation and decontamination procedures for laboratory equipment moves. · Safely disconnect, transport, and reinstall sensitive instrumentation, and confirm equipment function after each move. · Evaluate equipment condition for disposal decisions and execute decontamination and decommissioning procedures in compliance with environmental and safety regulations. · Coordinate equipment disposal or surplus through the appropriate channel, including recycling, hazardous waste, and remarketing. · Tag, photograph, document, and gather all required data for laboratory equipment, and remove retired instruments from asset management systems. · Track equipment performance metrics, monitor service histories, and maintain comprehensive asset records using computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS). · Provide technical input for replacement planning and capital budgeting based on equipment condition and performance data. · Diagnose equipment malfunctions and coordinate with external service vendors when specialized support is needed. · Support and coordinate with contractors on activities impacting lab space, and communicate operational updates to stakeholders. · Maintain installation records, move logs, retirement certificates, maintenance histories, manuals, and asset tracking information. · Maintain safe handling practices throughout all equipment installation, move, and retirement activities. Scope of Support · Laboratory and facility equipment installations, relocations, upgrades, modifications, and retirements. · Utility connections supporting laboratory and facility equipment, including electrical, gas, water, and data. · Contractor coordination, site access planning, and required escorts. · Equipment decommissioning, disposal, and surplus coordination, including recycling, hazardous waste, and remarketing channels. · Asset data coordination needed to preserve record integrity and CMMS compliance. · Move documentation, decontamination procedures, and post-move confirmation. Preferred Qualifications · Experience in life sciences, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, research, or other regulated facilities. · Knowledge of GMP, EHS, and quality expectations applicable to assigned work. · Certified Maintenance Technician, CMRT, or other relevant technical or reliability credential. · Experience supporting laboratory equipment lifecycle activities and multi-trade utility installations. · Familiarity with asset management and CMMS/EAMS data governance. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities · Strong mechanical and electrical troubleshooting skills across a range of laboratory equipment types. · Clear written and verbal communication with technical and nontechnical stakeholders. · Ability to follow calibration standards, validation protocols, and laboratory safety and decontamination procedures. · Customer-focused problem solving and professional vendor and contractor coordination. · Ability to manage multiple concurrent activities while maintaining attention to safety, quality, and compliance. · Sound judgment, proactive escalation, and disciplined record keeping. · Ability to work collaboratively across matrixed account and client teams.
